label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 13 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was recreated at 16:21:50Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. That handler INSERTs a new transaction for every provider-events message and never checks whether the event_id was already booked. The provider redelivers webhooks, and webhook-receiver publishes each delivery as its own Kafka message. So each redelivery after 16:21:50Z became a second or third balanced ledger posting. ledger_balanced still passes, but posted_exactly_once fails on 7 events and matches_provider fails on the provider_clearing total and on each affected payment. The duplicates net exactly to the reported gap: 3709 + 9533 + 4444 + 1827 + 5879 + 2×13193 = 51778 cents. The duplicated refund of 2455 cents is subtracted, giving 49323 cents, or +$493.23. payment-confirmer is idempotent (already_confirmed), so payments and refunds still match the provider.

evidence.shows: posted_exactly_once failed. Six events were posted twice and evt_000308 ($131.93) three times. The amounts net to +49323 cents, matching matches_provider's +$493.23 (ledger 1550150 vs provider 1500827). pay_000217 is -2455, from the doubled refund evt_000288. ledger_balanced, payments_match_provider and refunds_match_provider passed. Duplicate transaction ids run from 251 to 297.
ledger-consumer was recreated at 16:21:50Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, 17s before the alert. Every other service was created at 16:20:23Z and has not changed since.

evt_000251 was posted at 16:21:50.833Z (2@73) and again at 16:21:51.444Z (2@76), right after the recreate. Its transactions are 251 and 255, the lowest duplicate ids, so the other duplicates (ids 262 to 297) fall later, assuming ids are sequential.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000308 three times, from offsets 0@100, 0@101 and 0@103, between 16:22:04.3Z and 16:22:05.8Z.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000308 three times, once per delivery, at offsets 100, 101 and 103. Redeliveries reach Kafka as separate messages.
For offset 101, payment-confirmer returned already_confirmed. ledger-consumer returned posted, and its only queries were INSERTs into transactions and entries, with no lookup of the event_id first.
Before the recreate, ledger-consumer logged 'already processed' for repeats. The last one is at 16:21:48.605Z, and there are none after 16:21:50Z in a window that runs to 16:22:48Z.
The ledger already_processed rate falls off after the recreate while posted rises. The rate values are 1m extrapolated increases, so the tail values still reflect skips from before the recreate.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to the settings it ran before the 16:21:50Z deploy. That should be the deduplicating handler, but c2 does not show the earlier value of LEDGER_HANDLER; the deploy log does. This stops new duplicate postings. As a separate, human-run data repair, reverse or remove the extra transactions: 255, 266, 272, 273 and 297, the later of each pair for evt_000298, and two of the three for evt_000308 (ids not listed in c1). Then rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The ledger-consumer container is recreated, so ledger posting pauses briefly and resumes from its committed offsets. payment-confirmer, payments-api and webhook-receiver are not touched. If the earlier settings were also bad in some way, that behaviour comes back; the earlier value of LEDGER_HANDLER has not been seen. The rollback does not repair the 8 duplicate postings already in the ledger, so the money check keeps failing until the data repair is done.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Recreate ledger-consumer with the current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter) through a normal deploy. Avoid this unless the rollback breaks posting entirely, because naive mode books every redelivery again.
